name: Role Prompting
executive_summary: Assign the model a specific role or persona before the actual task — a simple, extremely widely-used technique shown to measurably improve zero-shot reasoning performance on top of just the role framing alone.
description: One of the most common prompting practices in casual use, formalized and measured academically: prepending a role assignment changes not just tone but measured task accuracy, including on reasoning benchmarks — the role framing shown to elicit more careful, systematic reasoning even without additional exemplars. Distinct from ExpertPrompting (already in this catalog): plain Role Prompting typically uses a single fixed, hand-written role description, while ExpertPrompting automatically generates a tailored, instruction-specific expert identity per query using in-context learning.
when_to_use: Zero-shot tasks where framing the response as coming from a specific relevant role plausibly improves depth, tone, or reasoning care — and a single fixed role (not per-instruction generation) is sufficient.
when_not_to_use: Tasks where a role framing would be misleading about the assistant's actual capabilities or credentials.
Cases needing a different, tailored persona per instruction — see ExpertPrompting instead.
known_pitfalls: A mismatched or overly narrow role can bias the response toward that role's assumed perspective even when a more general answer would serve the user better.

primary_source.authors: Kong, Zhang, Wang, Chen, Yin, Zhang, Zhang, Liu, Liu, Huang
primary_source.title: Better Zero-Shot Reasoning with Role-Play Prompting

variables.name: role_description
variables.example: a senior software architect reviewing a pull request for security issues

variables.name: task
variables.description: The actual task to perform in that role

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: A single LLM call (or a fixed sequence of them) with no external system dependency; running this template again at temperature 0 against the same model version should reproduce the same output.
